hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $y=-2x$

This line goes through the center of the rhombus and two of the corner points $(-2,4)$ and $(2,-4)$. 

Under this transformation, each point on the rhombus maps to another point which is also on the rhombus. The rhombus is *symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A rhombus mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The center of the rhombus is at the origin. The rhombus has a point at negative eight, negative four, a point at negative two, four, a point at two, negative four, and a point at eight, four. The equation y equals negative two X is graphed on the coordinate plane. An orange line with arrows show the image of the rhombus when reflected over the graphed line. The image maps over the pre-image.

##Reflection over $y=\dfrac{1}{2}x$

This line goes through the center of the rhombus and two of the corner points $(8,4)$ and $(-8,-4)$. 

Under this transformation, each point on the rhombus maps to another point which is also on the rhombus. The rhombus is *symmetric* over this line.


[[☃ image 1]]

The equation y equals one half X is graphed on the coordinate plane. A orange line with arrows show the image of the rhombus when reflected over the graphed line. The image maps over the pre-image.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the rhombus are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=-2x$ | Yes
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=\dfrac{1}{2}x$ | Yes
